output:
## Scope

`base` (`99cc3680`) → `HEAD` (`6d018934`) — one commit, `fix(review): reduce CodeRabbit pause friction`. 16 files, ~348 insertions / 36 deletions; ~90 non-test source lines (`scripts/pr/*.mjs`), ~130 test lines, the rest docs/config. Working tree clean apart from untracked `.skill/`.

I reviewed this myself. I did **not** use the second-model side channel — `gh` is disabled in this environment, and the change is small enough to hold in one pass; flagging that as a coverage gap rather than a choice I'd defend on a normal-sized PR.

---

## Verdict: does not pass yet

One blocking item, and it is the whole point of the change: I could not establish that `codeRabbitReviewSignal` can ever reach `reviewed` in production, and the repo's own recorded evidence argues against it for the clean-run case. If that holds, the feature is inert in the failing direction — it posts a manual review request on every PR.

---

## Fix before merge

### 1. `reviewed` may be unreachable, which inverts the change's purpose — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:766`

`classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal` reaches `reviewed` only when `isCurrentReviewSignal` is true, and with a non-null `currentHeadOid` that reduces to `reviewCommitOid(review) === currentHeadOid` (`:658`). `pr.reviews` arrives verbatim from `gh pr view --json ...,reviews` (`scripts/pr/pr-ready-state.mjs:756-775`) and is never enriched before `summarizeReadyState` (`:848-856`). To my knowledge gh's GraphQL `PullRequestReview` JSON exposes `id/author/authorAssociation/body/state/submittedAt/includesCreatedEdit/reactionGroups` and **no commit field** — in which case `reviewCommitOid` returns `null` for every real review and the comparison is always false.

**Unconfirmed** — `gh` is disabled here so I could not dump a real payload. But the code carries the tell: `reviewCommitOid` accepts four shapes (`commit.oid`, `commit.sha`, `commitId`, `commit_id`), which is what you write when you are unsure which one arrives, and every fixture in `pr-ready-state.test.mjs` hand-adds one. No test uses a recorded gh payload.

Consequence if it holds: a genuine exact-head CodeRabbit run classifies `stale`, `fallbackAction` stays `request_review_once_for_head_after_optional_check`, and babysit posts `@coderabbitai review` at closeout on **every** PR — one wasted round per PR on the Pro+ ladder and an "already reviewed, no new changes" reply. That is the friction the commit title claims to remove, and it contradicts the ADR's spend argument at `docs/adr/0066-...md:213-218`.

Remedy: dump `gh pr view <n> --json reviews` on a PR CodeRabbit has reviewed, before merging. If `commit` is absent, fetch review commits from `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/reviews` (REST returns `commit_id`, which `reviewCommitOid` already handles) and pass those in, and pin one fixture to the real payload.

### 2. A clean CodeRabbit run has no `**Run ID**` review and will be re-requested — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:762`

The loop only inspects `reviews` and requires `/\*\*Run ID\*\*:\s*`…`/`. The only recorded observation of real CodeRabbit output in this repo — `scripts/pr/pr-feedback-state.test.mjs:3354-3372`, explicitly labelled "the shapes observed on PR #1918, the first PR CodeRabbit reviewed in this repo" — shows the clean completion as a **top-level walkthrough comment** carrying `No actionable comments were generated in the recent review. 🎉` and `**Review profile**: CHILL`, with no Run ID and no review record. Repo-wide, `**Run ID**` appears *only* in this change's own code, test, and docs.

So on a PR where CodeRabbit ran clean against the exact head, the signal is `missing`/`stale` and babysit posts a redundant request. This is the same defect the other reviewer raised as its third point; their reasoning was speculative, but the repo's own fixture backs it.

**Partly confirmed**: the fixture is confirmed in-repo. Whether CodeRabbit *also* emits a zero-finding review record alongside the walkthrough is unverified.

Remedy: same verification pass as #1 — check both a clean and a with-findings run. If the clean form is walkthrough-only, accept the bounded walkthrough shape (`summarize by coderabbit.ai` marker + a current-head binding) as `reviewed`.

---

## Follow-up, not blocking

### 3. The change pushes `pr-ready-state-core.mjs` past the file-size cap — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:750-790`

**Confirmed by running the repo's own reporter.** `node scripts/repo-health/file-size-watchlist.mjs`:

```
| 961 | 1077 | +84 | near hard cap | scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs |
```

`docs/notes/file-size-watch.md:53` has it at `888 | 993 | soft cap`. Raw is now over the 1,000-line hard cap (`docs/pr-checklists/code-health.md:176-178`), and per `docs/notes/file-size-watch.md:20-24` the monthly workflow opens or updates a marked issue specifically for near-hard rows. The file is not on the exempt table.

Remedy: extract the review-signal classifiers (`isCodeRabbitFinalHeadReviewRequestBody`, `classifyCodeRabbitReviewSignal`, `classifyCodexReviewSignal`, `isCurrentReviewSignal`, `reviewCommitOid`) into a sibling module, or add the row to `docs/notes/file-size-watch.md` so it doesn't read as new drift.

### 4. The authority doc orders the closeout after the final pair; the three docs that defer to it say before — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:399`

`docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md` runs the projection pair at step 5 and posts the closeout at step 8, then all-clears at step 10. But `docs/notes/pr-operating-card.md:156-157` says "Before the final pair, apply the CodeRabbit exact-head request rule", both `babysit-pr/SKILL.md:295` copies say "before the final projection pair", and `ship/SKILL.md:214` says the same — all citing `pr-ready-state.md` as the owner of the contract. Read literally, the authority doc lets an agent all-clear on projections taken before the request went out.

The doc does already cover the late-finding case at `:123-125` ("If a requested review finishes while the PR is still under watch, rerun `pr:feedback-state`"), so this is an ordering inconsistency, not a missing rule.

Remedy: move the step-8 block ahead of step 5, or make step 10 name the re-run explicitly.

### 5. Canonical JSON example missing the new fields — `docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:276-306`

The example's `gates` block omits `codeRabbitReviewSignal` and the top-level `codeRabbitReviewSignal` sits next to `"codexReviewSignal": "in_flight"` at `:305`, while the field-expectations bullet at `:351` documents both. Confirmed. A consumer reading the example as the shape contract misses the field.

### 6. Marker comments are accepted from any author — `scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-786`

The `issueComments` loop checks only the body, not the author or association. On a public PR anyone can post `@coderabbitai review` plus the marker, flipping the state to `requested` and suppressing the legitimate closeout.

I'd rate this lower than the other reviewer did. It mirrors the pre-existing `classifyCodexReviewSignal` at `:707-731`, which is equally ungated, and the gate is `required: false` — the worst case is a skipped advisory review, not a bypassed required gate. The repo does have `isTrustedHumanAuthor` / `HUMAN_OVERRIDE_ASSOCIATIONS` (`:498-501`) if you want to gate it; do it for both classifiers or neither.

Related, same lines: a human typing the bare `@coderabbitai review` resume command named in `.coderabbit.yaml:64` carries no marker, so it's invisible here and babysit will post a second request on top of it.

### 7. "Idempotent" overstates the mechanism — `babysit-pr/SKILL.md:311` (both copies), `ship/SKILL.md:214`

GitHub has no conditional-create for issue comments, so check-then-post is best-effort duplicate suppression, not idempotency. Wording only.

---

## Considered and discarded

- **Adding a non-ready gate breaks readiness.** It doesn't — `gates` never feeds `requiredBlockers` generically; only `codexDescriptionApproval` pushes a blocker (`:1028-1036`), and `codeRabbitReviewSignal` is `required: false`. `summarizeFeedbackState`'s `ready` (`pr-feedback-state-core.mjs:542-547`) also names its three gates explicitly.
- **`formatHuman`/`formatCompact` printing `undefined`.** Both summary producers set the field, including the terminal path (`:828`), and the new test asserts no `undefined` in either format.
- **`pr:feedback-state` not surfacing the gate to the agent.** The CLI always emits JSON (`pr-feedback-state.mjs:11`), so `gates.codeRabbitReviewSignal` is readable as the skill instructs.
- **The `.agents/` ↔ `.claude/` mirrors drifting.** All three changed pairs are byte-identical.
- **Stale `auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits: 2` references.** None remain; `.coderabbit.yaml:66`, the pin, and both ADR mentions all say 5.
- **Step renumbering breaking cross-references.** The only `step 8` reference in the repo (`pr-operating-card.md:189`) points at the operating card's own list, which wasn't renumbered.
- **Other review's "require a head SHA" (its point 2).** Wrong on both halves. On the request path, `currentHeadOid` *is* passed and compared (`:777`). And `currentHeadOid = pr.headRefOid ?? …` (`:875`) with `headRefOid` in the fetch field list (`pr-ready-state.mjs:763`), so the timestamp fallback in `isCurrentReviewSignal` is unreachable on the production path.
- **Other review's "recheck the head before posting" (its point 4).** `babysit-pr/SKILL.md:300-301` already says "re-resolve and validate the full 40-hex `headRefOid`, then post this body". A residual TOCTOU window exists but the instruction is there.
- **The rewritten config test being a tautology.** It still guards against a coordinated bump of both the pin and the YAML, so it's narrower than the old range check but not vacuous.

## What I could not do

- `gh` is disabled in this environment, so findings 1 and 2 rest on code reading plus in-repo fixtures, not on a real payload. **Both need one live check before merge.**
- `node scripts/coderabbit-config.test.mjs` could not run — `js-yaml` is not installed in this checkout. The `.coderabbit.yaml` ↔ `EXPECTED_CONFIG` pin is therefore **unverified by execution**; I checked by hand that both sides say 5 and nothing else drifted.
- I did not observe CodeRabbit's actual review-body or walkthrough output; ADR 0066's post-rollout pause sample (16-of-29 PRs) is the author's claim and I did not reproduce it.

## Proof still owed

`node scripts/pr/pr-ready-state.test.mjs` (82 passed) and `node scripts/pr/pr-feedback-state.test.mjs` (51 passed) both pass — but every CodeRabbit fixture in them is hand-authored, so the green suite says the classifier does what its author intended, not that it matches GitHub or CodeRabbit. Outstanding before merge: run `pnpm agent:quality-gate --run` for the batch, dump `gh pr view --json reviews` on a CodeRabbit-reviewed PR, and exercise one clean and one with-findings run end to end.
other_review:
The exact-head closeout projection accepts untrusted or unbound signals and misses a valid CodeRabbit completion form. The workflow documentation also permits stale final projections and overstates duplicate suppression.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Reject untrusted closeout marker comments — /private/tmp/fx-1990/scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-774
  On a public PR, any outside commenter can post the command and current-head marker. This loop does not check the comment author or association, so it returns `requested` and prevents the babysitter from posting the legitimate closeout request. Accept markers only from an `OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`, or a recognized repository agent.

- [P2] Require a head SHA before accepting a review — /private/tmp/fx-1990/scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:766-767
  When `headRefOid` is unavailable, `isCurrentReviewSignal` falls back to a timestamp and can classify an unbound CodeRabbit review as `reviewed`; the request path similarly accepts a marked SHA without comparing it to a current head. Because this gate claims exact-head evidence, it must fail closed as `missing` or `stale` unless a full current head SHA is available.

- [P2] Recognize CodeRabbit clean-summary completions — /private/tmp/fx-1990/scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:772-774
  CodeRabbit can finish an exact-head clean run by updating a top-level summary instead of creating a non-empty review record. This loop inspects issue comments only for the manual-request marker, so a trusted summary with a Run ID and full reviewed commit range remains `missing` or `stale`, causing a redundant request and an “Already reviewed” response. Recognize the bounded trusted clean-summary form with head and timestamp checks.

- [P2] Recheck the head immediately before posting — /private/tmp/fx-1990/.agents/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:300-302
  If another push lands after this head lookup but before `gh pr comment`, the marker names the old head while the unbound CodeRabbit command reviews the then-current head. The projection can then miss the actual request and send another one. Re-read `headRefOid` immediately before the write and require it to equal the marker head.

- [P2] Treat the marker as best-effort duplicate suppression — /private/tmp/fx-1990/.agents/skills/babysit-pr/SKILL.md:310-312
  The marker does not make posting idempotent: two babysitters can both observe no marker and both create a comment before either write becomes visible, because GitHub issue comments have no conditional-create operation. Describe this as best-effort duplicate suppression and require a final refresh rather than promising idempotency.

- [P2] Extract review-signal logic from the near-hard core — /private/tmp/fx-1990/scripts/pr/pr-ready-state-core.mjs:750-755
  This classifier pushes `pr-ready-state-core.mjs` to 1,077 raw lines and 961 rough lines, an 84-line increase over the checked baseline and a near-hard result from the repository reporter. Extract the review-signal helpers into a focused module instead of extending this existing hotspot. See `docs/pr-checklists/code-health.md:176-183`.

- [P2] Add CodeRabbit fields to the canonical JSON example — /private/tmp/fx-1990/docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:351-355
  The field description introduces `codeRabbitReviewSignal`, but the preceding expected JSON example still omits both `gates.codeRabbitReviewSignal` and the top-level signal. Agents or consumers that use this canonical example will miss the new closeout state. Update the example as required by `AGENTS.md:90-95`.

- [P2] Run the final projections after the closeout request — /private/tmp/fx-1990/docs/notes/pr-ready-state.md:399-402
  The ordered workflow runs the projection pair in step 5 and posts the CodeRabbit request here in step 8, but step 10 does not explicitly require another pair afterward. If the requested review posts findings after the earlier sweep, the agent can report all-clear from stale projections. Move the request before the final pair or require both projections again after the closeout refresh, per `AGENTS.md:90-95`.
